structural_memory.memory: Shipboard HVAC and thermal service spans owner/manager, master, engineering/electro-technical crew, hotel/accommodation users, shore technical support, HVAC/refrigeration equipment or controls actors, yard and assurance roles. Equipment ownership, operating observation, comfort/service demand, support and modification history should remain distinct.

HVAC equipment readiness and delivered zone service are separate states. Installed or running equipment does not prove that every intended space receives adequate ventilation, heating or cooling, while a locally acceptable zone condition does not prove all central equipment is healthy.

Thermal and ventilation availability should preserve zone or service scope rather than collapsing to a vessel-wide binary. Accommodation, control/electronics spaces, machinery-related spaces and other intended services can have different availability at the same time.

Ventilation/airflow availability and heating/cooling availability are structurally different services. A space may retain air movement while thermal conditioning is degraded, or thermal equipment may be available while distribution or airflow to an affected zone is impaired.

Environmental-condition confidence is separate from HVAC command or equipment state. Historical memory can preserve whether a space condition was normal, degraded, uncertain or restored without retaining exact temperature, humidity, pressure or sensor thresholds.

Thermal demand/load and available heating/cooling capacity are separate clocks. Changing ambient conditions, occupancy or equipment heat load can alter service margin without proving a new equipment defect; exact loads, capacities and setpoints are deferred.

Thermal source or plant availability and distribution availability are distinct. Cooling/heating production may be available while an affected distribution path or zone service is unavailable, and downstream degradation should not automatically be attributed to the central plant.

HVAC degradation has a defensive lifecycle: observation, uncertain scope, affected-zone/service identification, degraded or unavailable state, temporary/local support state, restoration indication and post-restoration verification. No refrigerant, pressure, setpoint, control or troubleshooting procedure is retained.

Isolation or local-service state should remain bounded. One component, loop, distribution section or zone may be treated as unavailable while other HVAC service continues; exact ducts, piping, dampers, valves, controls and isolation actions are deferred.

HVAC redundancy should describe independent service paths or recoverability rather than simply counting units. Nominally multiple units can share electrical, distribution, control, cooling-medium, space or maintenance dependencies, so observed failover readiness and actual service continuity remain separate.

Thermal-management degradation can affect electronics/control spaces, machinery auxiliaries and other temperature-sensitive services, but downstream alarms or equipment problems are dependency observations rather than proof that HVAC was the root cause.

Accommodation ventilation/heating/cooling is a service-availability dimension that can affect habitability experience, but this blind pass does not convert environmental observations into medical, occupational-health or regulatory conclusions.

Restoration should preserve equipment return, distribution/airflow return, affected-zone condition confidence and downstream-service verification as potentially different timestamps. A restarted plant or cleared alarm does not by itself establish complete thermal-service recovery.

P070 electrical availability is an upstream dependency for many HVAC functions, but electrical service being present does not prove HVAC equipment readiness, distribution availability, zone service or environmental condition.

P067 equipment lifecycle should keep fan, compressor, pump, heat-exchange or controls equipment condition separate from delivered HVAC service; a sound component can coexist with a distribution/service problem, and acceptable zone conditions do not prove component condition.

P071 accommodation-service dependencies should keep freshwater and HVAC as independent utility dimensions. A habitability or hotel-service observation should not silently attribute cause to either utility without separate evidence.

P068 digital/control availability should separate HVAC control or sensor visibility from the physical thermal-service condition. Loss of monitoring/control visibility does not prove loss of heating/cooling, and a thermal problem does not establish a digital or cyber cause.
Equipment readiness, support, maintenance, commissioning and modification mechanics overlap the generic marine-equipment lifecycle recovered in P067.

Zone-scoped degradation, common-mode dependency, isolation and verified-restoration mechanics overlap the defensive service-state patterns recovered in P068-P071; P072 applies them specifically to HVAC and thermal service.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact vessel HVAC/refrigeration ducting, piping, zoning, equipment capacities, setpoints, refrigerants, pressures, temperatures, humidity limits, air-change rates and control logic are intentionally not retained.
Exact refrigerant handling, charging, pressure/temperature adjustment, controls tuning, isolation, troubleshooting, emergency or maintenance procedures are outside this blind pass.
Named HVAC/refrigeration OEMs, controls vendors, service firms, vessel installations, incidents, deficiencies and rule-specific findings require claim-scoped Evidence.
Private/regional marine HVAC/refrigeration integrator, controls, service and spares lineages plus historical non-English terminology remain deferred for source archaeology.
negative_space: Exact HVAC/refrigeration topology, capacities, setpoints, refrigerants, pressures, temperatures, humidity limits, air-change values and controls configuration.
Refrigerant handling, adjustment, isolation, troubleshooting, maintenance or emergency procedures.
Named equipment/providers, vessel incidents, deficiencies, assurance findings and current readiness.
Private/regional HVAC/refrigeration support lineages and non-English predecessor terminology.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive HVAC/ventilation/thermal-service orientation/source-discovery output. It is not HVAC, refrigeration, engineering, refrigerant-handling, controls, troubleshooting, health or vessel-operating advice and does not establish any exact topology, capacity, setpoint, refrigerant, pressure, temperature, humidity limit, procedure, equipment, provider, incident, compliance finding or current-readiness fact.
stop_reason: The shipboard HVAC/thermal lifecycle is recalled at useful structural resolution: equipment, zone scope, airflow/ventilation, heating/cooling, environmental confidence, demand, distribution, degradation, local support and verified restoration are separable states. Further detail would become vessel-, zone-, refrigerant-, pressure-, setpoint-, controls-, procedure-, incident-, provider- or jurisdiction-specific and is deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
